name: Intuned

modes.label: Standard browser machine, Developer plan overage
modes.note: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun (idle pool machines, incl. minCount, are not billed). $0.12/h beyond 100 included h; Large +$0.18/h, X-Large +$0.48/h surcharges metered separately in minutes (not covered by included hours). Standard 6 shared vCPU/2 GB, Large 8 shared vCPU/4 GB, X-Large 1 performance vCPU/8 GB. Runs max 6 h.

modes.label: Standard browser machine, Startup plan overage
modes.note: $0.1/compute-hour beyond the plan's included hours (intunedhq.com/pricing, 2026-09-28); metered in minutes. Machine CPU/RAM not published. Large +$0.15/h and X-Large +$0.40/h surcharges not modelled.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 3 included compute hours, no overage: trial only.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: 100 included compute hours (= $12 at $0.12/h); 25 API machines per workspace, 5 per project.

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: 500 included standard compute hours (= $50 at $0.10/h); 100 API machines per workspace, 15 per project; $40/mo AI credit (not compute).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom compute and machine limits, volume pricing, SSO/SAML, custom retention/regions/compliance.

features.ip_note: Managed proxy via intuned://auto (pool type not stated) or bring your own residential/datacenter/ISP proxy; stealth and CAPTCHA solving are experimental, platform-only, CAPTCHA solver needs headful mode; no per-GB price published.

caveats: Included standard compute 3/100/500 h; Developer excess $0.12/h, Startup $0.10/h. Large +$0.18/$0.15 per hour and XL +$0.48/$0.40. Job runs also $0.12/$0.10 beyond 100/400. API machine count is provisioned pool, not necessarily browser concurrency. Pricing and docs disagree on AI credit allowances; keep them separate from compute.
No invented browser vCPU or memory allocation: normalized 4/8 rate remains null. Proxy traffic is not necessarily equivalent to sandbox egress.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Re-checked 2026-09-28: per-hour compute rates are published (Developer $0.12/h, Startup $0.10/h beyond 100/500 included hours), so the card now prices a Standard machine per hour; machine size is unpublished (shown as a compromise).

JobRun overage is per JobRun (a batch execution), not per payload item: $0.12 (Developer) / $0.10 (Startup) per JobRun beyond 100/400 per month (Free: 10, hard limit). Compute hours are billed on top.
Per-project caps are tighter than the workspace total: max API machines per project/app 1 (Free), 5 (Developer), 15 (Startup); workspace 5/25/100. More needs support/Enterprise.
Billing thresholds: on paid plans Intuned can invoice usage mid-cycle when accrued usage hits an internal threshold; a failed threshold charge can pause the account (Unpaid).
AI usage billed through Intuned = model provider cost + 20% platform fee (BYOK avoids it). Plan fee is prorated at signup; billing anchored to the 1st; unused allowances do not roll over.

fleet.tiers: Workspace API-machine pool Free 5, Developer 25, Startup 100; per project/app 1/5/15 respectively. Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: 5 is API-machine provisioning capacity, not guaranteed total standalone browser/job concurrency. 10 in a single project needs Startup; 50 in one project exceeds all public per-project limits even though Startup workspace total is 100. 300/1,000 custom.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

own_agent_api.quote: lets you describe a web task in plain English and have it executed for you.
own_agent_api.note: Provider's own agent only: Web Tasks API (POST /{workspaceId}/web-tasks/start with task prompt, optional model haiku/sonnet/opus; then poll GET .../result). Start + poll only: no event streaming, no follow-up messages, no conversation resume documented. The hosted Intuned Agent (project builder) is a dashboard chat at app.intuned.io/agent; the 'External agent' is a Claude Code/Codex plugin run locally (private preview), not an API into the hosted machine. No API to drive Claude Code/Codex inside Intuned machines.

harness_api.quote: lets you describe a web task in plain English and have it executed for you.
harness_api.note: Provider's own agent only: Web Tasks API (POST /{workspaceId}/web-tasks/start with task prompt, optional model haiku/sonnet/opus; then poll GET .../result). Start + poll only: no event streaming, no follow-up messages, no conversation resume documented. The hosted Intuned Agent (project builder) is a dashboard chat at app.intuned.io/agent; the 'External agent' is a Claude Code/Codex plugin run locally (private preview), not an API into the hosted machine. No API to drive Claude Code/Codex inside Intuned machines.

secret_proxy.quote: Environment variables let you pass sensitive information—API keys, passwords, authentication tokens—to your Projects without exposing them in your code.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are project/workspace env vars read by the automation code; AuthSession credentials are stored by Intuned (or fetched from 1Password) and passed to your create/login code. No injecting proxy. Model spend for the Intuned agent/Web Tasks is platform-billed (AI credits), i.e. no user LLM key in the machine, but that is not a user-configurable credential proxy.

image_oci.quote: A Project contains your browser automation APIs and shared logic—written in Python or TypeScript using Playwright.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — you deploy code (Python/TypeScript) into managed browser machines, not a custom Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: A Project is both your automation code and your runtime environment.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a code-first browser automation platform; no documented ability to run Docker/containers inside the machine.

nested_virt.quote: A Project is both your automation code and your runtime environment.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no /dev/kvm or nested VM/emulator capability is documented for browser machines.

desktop.quote: Websites block automated traffic by examining browser fingerprints... Intuned provides four features to help your automations avoid detection: proxies, headful mode, stealth mode, and CAPTCHA solving.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — offers headful/headless browser execution and traces, not a general graphical desktop (VNC/RDP/stream).

computer_use.quote: lets you describe a web task in plain English and have it executed for you.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Web Tasks/Intuned Agent drive a browser via generated code/AI, not a screenshot+click computer-use API, and there is no desktop to drive.

egress_ip_type.quote: Residential | IPs from real ISP users | Per GB (expensive)... Datacenter | IPs from cloud data centers | Per IP/month... ISP | Datacenter-hosted but ISP-registered
egress_ip_type.note: Both a managed proxy pool (intuned://auto, pool type unstated) and user-supplied residential/datacenter/ISP proxies are supported; underlying default egress type without a proxy is not stated.

ssh.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — automations are invoked via API/CLI/online IDE; no SSH access into the browser machine is documented.

snapshot.quote: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun (idle pool machines, incl. minCount, are not billed).
snapshot.note: Browser machines are ephemeral per Run/JobRun; no snapshot/checkpoint (disk or memory) feature is documented.

snapshot_auto.quote: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun.
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no automatic state save/restore on stop/sleep is documented.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun.
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no API/CLI checkpoint action is documented.

fork.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine cloning feature is documented; concurrency is handled via pooled API machines, not forking.

fork_running.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

pause_resume.quote: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun (idle pool machines, incl. minCount, are not billed).
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — machines are provisioned/torn down per Run/JobRun; no explicit pause/resume of a single machine is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Runs — On-demand execution via API. You trigger a Run, we handle queuing and concurrency.
wake_on_request.note: Calling the Run/Job API automatically provisions a browser machine on demand; there is no separate explicit start/wake call for a specific machine.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Compute is billed only while a machine executes a Run/JobRun (idle pool machines, incl. minCount, are not billed).
auto_stop_idle.note: Machines are torn down/idled automatically outside of active Run/JobRun execution.

persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser machines are ephemeral per Run/JobRun; persistence is via an app-level KV store (persistentStore/attemptStore) and AuthSessions, not a filesystem/disk that survives stop/start.

volume_attach.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no attachable persistent volume feature is documented.

volume_shared.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

live_resize.quote: Standard 6 shared vCPU/2 GB, Large 8 shared vCPU/4 GB, X-Large 1 performance vCPU/8 GB.
live_resize.note: Machine size (Standard/Large/X-Large) is chosen per Run/Job; no documented way to resize CPU/RAM of an already-running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: Run the Intuned agent locally in your own coding agent instead of the hosted agent... Supported in Claude Code and Codex.
agent_harnesses.note: The Claude Code/Codex integration is a plugin you run locally against your own project files (private preview), not a coding harness preinstalled inside an Intuned-hosted sandbox/machine.

mcp_server.quote: Introduction, Quickstarts, Intuned Agent overview, Web Tasks, CLI, Runtime SDKs...
mcp_server.note: not offered: no MCP server for controlling Intuned sandboxes/machines is listed in the documentation index or found elsewhere on the site.

lang_python.quote: a Project contains your browser automation APIs and shared logic—written in Python or TypeScript using Playwright.

lang_node.quote: a Project contains your browser automation APIs and shared logic—written in Python or TypeScript using Playwright.

public_ipv4.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser machines are reached only through the Intuned API (Runs/Jobs/Web Tasks), not via a dedicated public IPv4 address.

inbound_https.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no feature to expose an inbound HTTPS URL to a port on the browser machine.

ingress_rules.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no inbound-reachable surface on machines to control access to.

egress_allowlist.quote: Anywhere a proxy is accepted for runs, AuthSessions, jobs, Web Tasks, or project defaults, pass either: A proxy URL string... A non-empty array of ordered proxy rule objects.
egress_allowlist.note: Proxy configuration lets you route/condition outbound requests through a proxy, but there is no documented allow/deny egress list or no-internet mode.

egress_http_rules.quote: Add regex to proxy only requests whose URL matches an RE2 pattern... Intuned matches against the request URL's scheme, host, and percent-encoded pathname.
egress_http_rules.note: The regex proxy-routing rule matches on URL path but only decides which upstream proxy to use, not a method/path-scoped allow/deny egress security control.

guest_firewall.quote: A Project is both your automation code and your runtime environment.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — machines are managed browser runtimes without documented root/shell access, so no nftables/iptables control inside is available (derived).

static_egress_ip.quote: Intuned resolves this to a working proxy from its managed pool at run time, health-checking candidates automatically.
static_egress_ip.note: Default managed proxy resolves from a pool (not fixed); a fixed/static IP is only achievable by bringing your own dedicated datacenter/ISP proxy, not a native Intuned static egress IP.

gpu.quote: Standard 6 shared vCPU/2 GB, Large 8 shared vCPU/4 GB, X-Large 1 performance vCPU/8 GB.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only CPU/RAM machine sizes for browser automation are offered; no GPU machines.

windows.quote: Standard machine, Large machine, X-Large machine
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser machines run Linux (Playwright-based); no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: Standard machine, Large machine, X-Large machine
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machine option is documented.

self_host.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Intuned is a hosted SaaS platform; no self-hosted deployment option is documented.

byoc.quote: Custom compute and machine limits, volume pricing, SSO/SAML, custom retention/regions/compliance.
byoc.note: Enterprise offers custom regions/compliance/retention, but a bring-your-own-cloud-account managed deployment is not documented.

open_source.quote: Intuned handles the infrastructure: browser provisioning, execution queues, retries, and scaling.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Intuned is a proprietary hosted platform; client SDKs (e.g. @intuned/client) are npm/pip packages but the core platform is not open source.

isolation.quote: When you deploy a project, the code, dependencies, and configurations are built, packaged, and deployed on dedicated virtual machines.
isolation.note: Docs describe per-project pools of dedicated VMs; each machine handles one Run at a time 'to ensure full isolation'. Underlying hypervisor (e.g. KVM/Firecracker) not disclosed, so mapped to the generic dedicated-vm category rather than a specific hypervisor.

arm64.quote: Standard machine 6 shared vCPU/2 GB, Large machine 8 shared vCPU/4 GB, X-Large machine 1 performance vCPU/8 GB
arm64.note: not offered: pricing/docs list only three fixed x86-style machine sizes for the Chromium browser workload, with no ARM/Apple-silicon architecture option or mention anywhere in the docs (llms-full.txt) or pricing page.

eu_data_residency.quote: The region where your Intuned project is hosted. **Available regions:** * "nl": Netherlands * "de": Germany * "fr": France * "se": Sweden * "es": Spain * "ro": Romania * "pl": Poland * "gb": United Kingdom
eu_data_residency.note: Project config lets you pin the hosting region to several EU member states (Netherlands, Germany, France, Sweden, Spain, Romania, Poland), among other regions.
